sentences.text: Shri Hemant Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A. for the State are present.
No one appears on behalf of opposite party no. 2, though notice has been served upon him.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 13.09.2021 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST) Act, Bulandshahar, whereby the learned Judge has rejected the appellant's Bail Application No. 3971 of 2021, arising out of Complaint Case No. 31 of 2019, under Sections 420,
406, 323, 427, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(D) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Sikandrabad, District Bulandshahar.

sentences.text: At the time of filing of the complaint Rs. 12 lacs were due against the appellant-accused and three other co-accused persons.
On the demand being made by the complainant, co-accused Naipal Singh on 30.06.2018 gave him a cheque of Rs. one lac drawn on HDFC Bank.
When the complainant deposited the cheque, it was dishonored due to insufficient balance in the account.
Later on there was an agreement between the appellant and complainant on 19.11.2018 that they will return the money due in six installments.
But they did not pay any of the installments.

On 20.02.2018, co-accused Naipal Singh gave a cheque of Rs. 50,000/- signed by him to the complainant but on presentation for encashment, it was bounced as there was no money in the accused's account.
On 15.02.2019 the appellant-accused called the complainant at Company Branch Office Sikandrabad.
When the complainant reached there, the accused persons hurled abuses relating to his caste and beat him by kicks and fists.
The accused persons threatened the complainant to dire consequences, in case he takes any step to return the money.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
It is submitted that the cheque was not issued by the appellant, it was issued by co-accused Naipal Singh.
It is also submitted that the appellant is respectable citizen having no criminal history to his credit.
It is in the last submitted that the appellant is in jail since 05.08.2021 and in case he is released on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant, but could not dispute the aforesaid factum of the case as argued by the learned counsel for the appellant.

Considering the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, facts and circumstances of the case,
nature of the offence, evidence appearing in the case, the period of incarceration undergone by the appellant, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.
The impugned order dated 13.09.2021 rejecting the bail application of the appellant is hereby set aside.

Let the appellant Aas Khan alias Aas Mohammad be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) That the appellant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

It is made clear that in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the appellant.
